findings.reason: without a fixture whose delay covers the cited 4 s (or a stated window length), the section's headline claim, that the retry covers a launch that starts slowly, is measured by nothing and the next node can satisfy its gate while leaving the incident unrepaired.
findings.text: the mechanism is "refusal text … within a bounded startup window sized for a placed step … or at a stated number of seconds", but the done-when's fixture only requires the fake bwrap to write the refusal "after a delay longer than 0.5 s", while the incident §19 is written to cover took ~4 s from `launched_at` 07:35:53Z to `exited_at` 07:35:57Z, and the window's other bound ("the first stream record") cannot fire for that shape at all because `stream.jsonl` is empty; an implementation choosing a one-second window passes every arm of the done-when and still records this launch as failed

findings.reason: the dispatch fences a node from the write paths the plan declares, and an undeclared scope invites a grant spanning the neighbouring launch modules (`reckon/_backends.py`, `reckon/host_shims/`) that §18 and §15 own.
findings.text: §19 states no "Write paths:" clause, names no test file and no gate-log path, where the eighteen sibling sections each end with "Write paths: …" (the nearest, §18 at `:1579`, names three modules and its test file), so the node's exclusive file scope must be guessed and its evidence path is undeclared

findings.reason: the prefix is unique in the runs root and one `ls` reaches the record, so the claim it supports (`ended_during: launch`, the refusal in `stderr.log`) is checkable; carrying the slug in every citation is house convention rather than a correctness fix.
findings.text: "Run `r-20261021T073526532476`" names a run by timestamp prefix alone and no directory resolves at `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261021T073526532476`; the record the section describes is at `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261021T073526532476-jt60sa-2023-shot-census`, and every other run id in this plan carries its slug

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the cited run is named by timestamp prefix only, and no directory resolves at that path; every other run id in the plan carries its slug suffix.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §19's window is left as "a stated number of seconds" while its fixture only requires a delay "longer than 0.5 s", so no arm fails for a window too short to cover the cited incident.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — §19 declares no write paths and names neither a test file nor a gate-log path, unlike every sibling section, so a later reader has no durable path to open and a dispatcher cannot derive the node's file scope.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name or ticket number reaches the symbols §19 names; it cites mechanisms (`_spawn_worker_retrying_a_vanished_bind`, `_died_over_a_vanished_bind_source`, `SANDBOX_STARTUP_WINDOW_SECONDS`) rather than its own identity.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause matches the cited record (launched 07:35:53Z to exit 07:35:57Z is ~4 s, past the 0.5 s window, and `stream.jsonl` is empty with the refusal in `stderr.log`), and both callers the mechanism must run under are named and do call the retry (`reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:1606`, `:2439`).
